To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the diagnosis of functional hypothalamic anovulation is not a simple one.

1) the presence of eating disorders is associated with a higher prevalence of functional hypothalamic hypogonadism; 2) the presence of functional hypothalami hypogonadisn is associated with a lower prevalence of eating disorders; 3) the presence of stress is associated with a high prevalence of functional hypothalamus hypogonadisma.

body cell mass, phase angle and leptin concentrations can be used as diagnostic markers of functional amenorrhea related primarily to energy deficiency, while cortisol and free T(3) levels may be used in subjects who have a history of stressful events.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying diagnostic criteria that can be used to distinguish between subjects with amenorrhea related largely to minimal energy deficiency from those in whom failure to adapt to stress prevails.
the study of a group of young women with secondary hypothalamic amenorrhoea and disordered eating.

the development of a diagnostic algorithm that integrates body composition variables and endocrine parameters in order to distinguish between subjects with amenorrhea related mainly to energy deficiency and those with failure of the adaptive response to stress.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a combination of body composition variables and leptins can help to distinguish the two groups of subjects with secondary amenorrheas.

the presence of a stress condition in the history is associated with a more marked reduction of lean body mass, and that leptin levels are a good marker of the presence of active lean compartment, and therefore of a better response to the stress condition.
in the presence of amenorrhea, a low BMI is associated with a high risk of eating disorders, and a low body cell mass with stress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a modest eating disorder is the most frequent cause of amenorrhea in young women, but that it is not the only one.

in young subjects with secondary amenorrheal, the assessment of body composition, especially of the lean mass component, may help to differentiate between those in whom the hypothalamic dysfunction is related to minimal energy deficit, and those who present failure of adaptive response.
a modest degree of energy deficiency, as measured by BMI, fat mass, leptin, and body cell mass, is associated with amenorrhea in the absence of other stressors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the study of body cell mass and its relationship to leptin and other endocrine parameters can help to distinguish between amenorrhea related mainly to energy deficiency and amenorrhea in which stress is the major factor.
body composition analysis, including phase angle measured by BIA, is a valid tool to identify subjects with functional hypothalamus amenorrhea and disordered eating.

a combination of anthropometric, body composition and biochemical variables is a useful tool for distinguishing between subjects with functional amenorrhea related mostly to minimal energy deficiency from those with failure of adaptive response.
